sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's 2025-2030 RUPTL revision prioritizes geothermal and bioenergy baseload capacity, creating a multi-year order book for PGEO and CDIA independent of global rate cycles.
Domestic renewable IPPs with captive industrial off-takers (MPOW, TPIA) are structurally insulated from export-market price volatility, unlike US-listed climate-tech peers.
The widening ID-US spread in renewables signals a policy-driven re-rating of Indonesian clean-energy assets, favoring local-currency revenue streams over dollar-denominated growth stories.
sectors.ai: Buy selective geothermal and bioenergy names (PGEO, CDIA, MPOW) on Indonesia's 2030 baseload-renewables mandate, but trim exposure to US-linked climate-tech (NRG, 373220) until the Fed pivot is clearer. The sector's local outperformance (+0.59% vs -2.17% US) confirms domestic policy momentum is the only durable bid; rotate into names with PPA visibility and avoid speculative hydrogen plays.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Small/mid-cap FMCG names are driving sector returns as institutional investors rotate out of large-cap staples into higher-beta consumer plays with clearer earnings catalysts.
Water and beverage companies (ADES, AGAR) are benefiting from structural demand growth in premium hydration and on-the-go consumption, supported by rising urban disposable income.
Packaging and plastics-linked consumer firms (PDES, INDR) are gaining on input-cost stabilization and export-driven volume recovery, offering durable margin expansion into 2025.
sectors.ai: Buy selective small/mid-cap FMCG names showing volume-price breakouts (PDES, ADES, AGAR) while large caps lag; momentum is broad but fragile, so take profits on 10%+ single-day spikes. Favor water/beverage and packaging sub-sectors for earnings visibility; avoid chasing BTEK without confirmation. Position for a 2-4 week hold as IDX consumer breadth improves, but trim if aggregate signal flips negative.

SMGR's steady advance signals cement demand is firming ahead of the election-year infrastructure push. Trim US-exposed names like VRT on rate-cut delays; rotate into domestic contractors with visible government backlog.
